ctor.rationale: `base(3, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Ancient, TargetType.Self)` (Corruption.cs:21-24) == cost 3 / POWER / ANCIENT / SELF. Corruption has NO Exhaust keyword of its own -- the Exhaust hover tip (Corruption.cs:19) describes what CorruptionPower does to Skills -- and the sim correctly leaves `exhausts` False.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- the sim passes the literal 1 (corruption.py:35)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new DynamicVar("Power", 1m)` (Corruption.cs:17) is a printed var with no `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so `magic_number` returns None. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no corresponding `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. DORMANT for game fidelity (the dealt/applied number is identical), LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<CorruptionPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["Power"].BaseValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (Corruption.cs:30) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, CorruptionPower, 1, applier=ctx.player)`. CorruptionPower's Skills-cost-0 and exhaust-on-play behaviour belongs to the power stream. Presentation, folded in: NPowerUpVfx (28) and TriggerAnim (29).
